title: Family Law
audience: a law student in a U.S. JD program
purpose: Analyze marriage and its alternatives, constitutional family rights, divorce, property division and spousal support, child support, custody and parenting time, parentage including assisted reproduction, adoption, protection orders, and interstate jurisdiction under the UCCJEA and UIFSA.

weeks.5: Property division: community property and equitable distribution
weeks.12: Interstate jurisdiction: the UCCJEA and UIFSA

blocks.deliverable: Decide whether a premarital agreement is enforceable.
Compare fault and no-fault grounds in a supplied case.
Divide a supplied marital estate under both systems.
Week 7 midterm; apply a percentage-of-income child-support model.
Determine legal parentage in three family arrangements.
Decide which state may hear a custody case under the UCCJEA.
Submit the project; take an unseen 180 minute final in week 14.

project: Divorce case file: for a supplied couple, analyze property division, support and custody, outline a proposed settlement agreement, and write a client letter explaining the likely outcomes.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.

files.L12.txt: Interstate jurisdiction: the UCCJEA and UIFSA
